A.explanation: Force in $\text{N}$ is a vector and upwards gives its direction alongside the $1 \text{ N}$ magnitude.

B.explanation: Mass in $\text{kg}$ is a scalar and decrease describes a change in magnitude, not a direction in space.

C.explanation: Temperature in $\text{K}$ is a scalar and cooler describes a temperature change, not a vector direction.

D.explanation: Time in $\text{s}$ is a scalar and later describes a time shift, not a vector direction.

hints: Look at the unit in each option: $\text{N}$, $\text{kg}$, $\text{K}$ and $\text{s}$ tell you whether the quantity is force, mass, temperature or time.
Recall that a vector needs both a magnitude with unit and a spatial direction, while words like decrease, cooler and later only describe a change.
Check which extra word is a true direction in space, such as upwards, and which quantity it is paired with.
walkthrough: A vector quantity is defined by magnitude and direction, while a scalar has magnitude only.
Check the quantities from the units: $\text{N}$ is force, $\text{kg}$ is mass, $\text{K}$ is temperature, $\text{s}$ is time.
Of these, force is a vector quantity, while mass, temperature and time are scalar quantities.
Only $1 \text{ N}$ upwards gives both a magnitude, $1 \text{ N}$, and a spatial direction, upwards.
The words decrease, cooler and later do not give a spatial direction, so they do not make a vector statement.
